facts.statement: Arackar is an extinct genus of lithostrotian sauropod that may belong to the family Saltasauridae.
facts.quote: Arackar (meaning "skeleton" in Kunza) is an extinct genus of lithostrotian sauropod, possibly part of the Saltasauridae

facts.statement: The holotype specimen was discovered in 1993 at Quebrada La Higuera, about 75 km south of Copiapó.
facts.quote: The holotype was discovered in 1993 at Quebrada La Higuera, approximately 75 km (47 mi) south of Copiapó

facts.statement: The species Arackar licanantay was named and described in 2021 by a team led by David Rubilar-Rogers.
facts.quote: In 2021, Arackar licanantay was named and described by David Rubilar-Rogers, Alexander O. Vargas, Bernardo González Riga, Sergio Soto-Acuña, Jhonatan Alarcón-Muñoz, José Iriarte-Díaz, Carlos Arévalo and Carolina S. Gutstein

facts.statement: The holotype fossil includes neck and back vertebrae, a humerus, a femur, and an ischium.
facts.quote: It includes vertebrae of the neck and back, as well as a humerus, femur and ischium

facts.statement: The holotype represents a juvenile individual and is the most complete sauropod specimen known from Chile.
facts.quote: It belonged to a juvenile and is currently the most complete specimen of a sauropod found in Chile

facts.statement: The holotype individual had an estimated body length of around 6.3 meters.
facts.quote: The holotype represents a small individual with a body length estimated at around 6.3 m long

facts.statement: The size of a fully grown Arackar is currently unknown.
facts.quote: The size of a fully grown Arackar is unknown

facts.statement: A distinctive feature of Arackar is a high and wide hollow between the prearticular process and the vertebral body.
facts.quote: El hueco entre la protuberancia antearticular y el cuerpo vertebral es alto y ancho

facts.statement: Arackar lived during the Late Cretaceous, approximately between 83.3 and 66 million years ago, in what is now South America.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente entre hace 83.3 y 66 millones de años entre el Campaniense y el Maastrichtiense, en lo que es hoy Sudamérica

facts.statement: The time range for Arackar spans from the Campanian to the Maastrichtian stages, from 83.6 to 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Maastrichtian (83.6 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: Arackar is classified within Titanosauria and Lithostrotia as a sister taxon to Isisaurus.
facts.quote: Arackar was placed in the Titanosauria within the Lithostrotia in 2021, as a sister taxon of Isisaurus

facts.statement: Arackar forms a clade with Rapetosaurus and is possibly part of the Saltasauridae family.
facts.quote: Arackar fue colocado en Titanosauria dentro de Lithostrotia, como taxón hermano de Isisaurus formando un clado junto con Rapetosaurus, posiblemente dentro de Saltasauridae

facts.statement: The holotype is currently the most complete sauropod specimen found in Chile.
facts.quote: Actualmente es el ejemplar más completo de saurópodo encontrado en Chile

facts.statement: Expeditions in 2006, 2007, and 2011 found an additional specimen preserved in similar conditions about 100 meters from the holotype.
facts.quote: Adicionalmente, se han hecho otras 3 expediciones al sitio en 2006, 2007 y 2011, resultando en el descubrimiento de un espécimen extra preservado en condiciones similares separado por unos 100 metros del holotipo

facts.statement: The species name licanantay translates to "bones of the Atacamans" in the Kunza language.
facts.quote: The full binomial name, Arackar licanantay, translates to "bones of the Atacamans" in the Kunza language
